title: Strict Monotonicity of the Weighted Power Mean Chain: WHM < WGM < WAM < WQM ⇔ a ≠ b
description: Answers the strict-monotonicity open question for the two-point weighted power mean chain. Off the diagonal a ≠ b, every link of WHM ≤ WGM ≤ WAM ≤ WQM is strict, and each strict gap is governed by the single scalar condition a ≠ b. The result is a rigidity dichotomy: either a = b and all four means coincide, or a ≠ b and every inequality is strict simultaneously — a single strict gap anywhere forces all of them. Each strict link is obtained by upgrading a non-strict inequality with the parent's equality characterization (= ⇔ a = b).

Builds on the parent sibling file (the equality case of the chain), which uses Mathlib's weighted AM-GM equality condition; the two remaining non-strict links are re-derived here from Mathlib's two-variable weighted AM-GM.

overview.historicalContext: The classical mean chain HM ≤ GM ≤ AM ≤ QM and its weighted generalization come with a sharp equality theory: equality holds throughout iff all arguments coincide. The strict form — every inequality is strict once the arguments differ — is the contrapositive content, and is exactly the two-point, weighted instance of the strict monotonicity of power means p ↦ M_p. Hardy, Littlewood and Pólya (Inequalities, 1934) give the strict-convexity argument behind the underlying weighted AM-GM equality case.
overview.problemStatement: The grandparent file proved the non-strict weighted chain WHM ≤ WGM ≤ WAM ≤ WQM, and the parent file characterized when each link is an equality (iff a = b). Are the inequalities strict off the diagonal, i.e. when a ≠ b?
overview.text: We prove that for positive reals a, b with positive weights w₁, w₂ summing to 1, every link of the chain is strict precisely when a ≠ b. Because all three equality conditions reduce to the same scalar condition a = b, the strict gaps appear and disappear together: there is no intermediate regime where some links are tight and others slack.
overview.proofStrategy: Each strict link is LE.le.lt_of_ne applied to (i) the non-strict inequality and (ii) the parent's equality characterization, whose contrapositive supplies the strict inequality whenever a ≠ b. The two harmonic/geometric ≤ links are re-derived inline from Mathlib's two-variable weighted AM-GM (so the file imports only the parent, not the grandparent), while the quadratic–arithmetic strict gap is reused directly from the parent's wam_lt_wqm_of_ne (positive weighted variance). Packaging each link as an iff (< ⇔ a ≠ b) via Iff.not yields the headline strict_chain_iff_ne and the rigidity dichotomy any_strict_iff_all_strict. The equal-weight corollary rewrites each mean into its textbook closed form.
keyInsights: Strictness needs no new analytic input: it is purely (non-strict inequality) + (equality characterization). The mathematical work was already done in the equality case; strictness is its logical shadow.
All three equality conditions collapse to the single scalar a = b, so the three strict gaps are equivalent to one another and to a ≠ b. This is what makes the dichotomy 'all or nothing'.
The rigidity statement any_strict_iff_all_strict has no analogue at the level of a bare inequality chain: it is a consequence of every link sharing the same equality locus.
Reusing sibling files (non-strict chain + equality case) rather than re-deriving keeps the file short and isolates the genuinely new content (the strict dichotomy).

The headline equivalence is really a statement about the equality locus: because all three links share the same locus {a = b}, strictness of the chain is governed by a single scalar invariant rather than three independent conditions. This is the two-point shadow of the strict monotonicity of the power-mean map p ↦ M_p, whose level sets degenerate only on the constant configurations.

conclusion.summary: Off the diagonal a ≠ b, every link of the weighted power mean chain WHM < WGM < WAM < WQM is strict, and each strict gap is equivalent to the single condition a ≠ b. Hence the chain obeys a rigidity dichotomy: all four means coincide (a = b) or all inequalities are strict (a ≠ b), with no intermediate regime — a single strict gap forces them all.
conclusion.implications: This sharpens the equality case into a full trichotomy-free picture of the chain: the equality locus of every link is the same diagonal a = b. In probabilistic terms (a, b with probabilities w₁, w₂), WAM < WQM ⇔ a ≠ b is positive variance of a non-constant two-point variable, and the dichotomy says the means degenerate together exactly when the variable is constant.
openQuestions: Does the same all-or-nothing rigidity hold for the n-variable weighted chain — is each strict link equivalent to 'the aᵢ are not all equal', and do all links become strict simultaneously?
Can the strict monotonicity be upgraded to a quantitative gap, e.g. a lower bound on WQM − WAM (or WAM − WGM) in terms of w₁w₂(a−b)², refining the qualitative strictness?
